newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA RETAIL TRADE - Review of expectations.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA RETAIL TRADE - Review of expectations.

text.p: Australian retail trade data for July will be released at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) today.
The median forecast os for a 0.4 percent rise in the month, following on from June's 0.1 percent rise.
Forecasts from the 32 economists Reuters surveyed ranged from a 0.5 percent fall to a 1.0 percent rise.
Of those surveyed, only three expected a negative result in July, with a further four expecting a flat result.
If the median forecast is realised, annual growth will slow to 4.4 percent, almost half the 8.6 percent recorded in January.
Recent data, and forecasts for July, are listed below.
Retail Trade Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul(f)
The data was delayed from last Friday, a move which has sparked some market rumours that the delay is due to the data showing quite a substantial movement.
With the economy seen going through a slow patch in the middle of the year, economists do not expect the data to show to much strength, but still expect it to be slightly positive.

Helping keep the forecasts down is the fact that the data will measure spending in the lead up to the August 20 budget, as consumers may have been affected by the press speculation on what the budget would contain.
Against that, the first effects of the rate cuts by some of the major banks may start to appear.

However the effects of the July 31 rate cut and susbsequent home loan rate rate reductions will have no impact on this data. As the data will be one of the first partial indicators of the September quarter, the July result will be important as it will help frame initial opinions of how the economy is performing after a flat June quarter.
Amid an environment where a majority of economists expect a rate cut in the fourth quarter, a weak result would fuel market speculation of a near term rate cut.
